content.title: Passive voice: processes, maps and impersonal statements
content.instructions: Rewrite each sentence following the cue. Leave out the agent (by …) when it is obvious or unimportant, as you would in a Task 1 process or map description. Write the complete new sentence.

items.prompt: First, workers pick the tea leaves by hand. (Use the passive and leave out the agent.)
accepted_answers: First, the tea leaves are picked by hand.
First, tea leaves are picked by hand.
items.model_answer: First, the tea leaves are picked by hand.
items.explanation: Process diagrams focus on what happens to the product, not on who does it, so the present simple passive (am/is/are + past participle) is the standard choice. 'Workers' is obvious and can be omitted; 'by hand' describes the method, not the agent, so it stays.

items.prompt: After the plant has sorted the bottles by colour, it melts them down. (Use the passive in both clauses.)
accepted_answers: After the bottles have been sorted by colour, they are melted down.
After being sorted by colour, the bottles are melted down.
After the bottles are sorted by colour, they are melted down.
items.model_answer: After the bottles have been sorted by colour, they are melted down.
items.explanation: The present perfect passive (have been + past participle) shows that one stage is complete before the next begins. Linking stages with after / once / when in this way is a clear sign of range in a Task 1 process answer.

items.prompt: Once the clay has been shaped, a kiln fires it at 1,000°C. (Use the passive in the second clause.)
accepted_answers: Once the clay has been shaped, it is fired in a kiln at 1,000°C.
Once the clay has been shaped, it is fired at 1,000°C in a kiln.
items.model_answer: Once the clay has been shaped, it is fired in a kiln at 1,000°C.
items.explanation: The object of the active verb (it = the clay) becomes the subject of the passive verb (is fired). A machine or place is usually expressed with 'in' or 'using' rather than 'by' in process descriptions.

items.prompt: Finally, the manufacturer packages the finished product and transports it to supermarkets. (Use the passive.)
accepted_answers: Finally, the finished product is packaged and transported to supermarkets.
Finally, the finished product is packaged and then transported to supermarkets.
items.model_answer: Finally, the finished product is packaged and transported to supermarkets.
items.explanation: When two passive verbs share the same subject, 'is' does not need to be repeated: 'is packaged and transported'. This keeps the final stage of a process concise.

items.prompt: Between 1990 and 2010, developers demolished the old factory and built a shopping centre in its place. (Use the passive.)
accepted_answers: Between 1990 and 2010, the old factory was demolished and a shopping centre was built in its place.
Between 1990 and 2010, the old factory was demolished and replaced by a shopping centre.
items.model_answer: Between 1990 and 2010, the old factory was demolished and a shopping centre was built in its place.
items.explanation: Map comparisons describe changes to buildings and places over a finished period, so they use the past simple passive (was/were + past participle). Because the two clauses have different subjects, 'was' must be repeated.

items.prompt: According to the plan, the council will convert the old warehouse into apartments. (Use the passive and leave out the agent.)
accepted_answers: According to the plan, the old warehouse will be converted into apartments.
According to the plan, the old warehouse is going to be converted into apartments.
items.model_answer: According to the plan, the old warehouse will be converted into apartments.
items.explanation: For proposed changes on a Task 1 map, use the future passive: will be + past participle. The agent (the council) is unimportant, so it is left out.

items.prompt: People widely accept that regular exercise reduces the risk of heart disease. Rewrite starting 'It is …'
accepted_answers: It is widely accepted that regular exercise reduces the risk of heart disease.
items.model_answer: It is widely accepted that regular exercise reduces the risk of heart disease.
items.explanation: The impersonal passive 'It is + past participle + that-clause' (It is believed / argued / widely accepted that …) presents a general view objectively, which suits a formal Task 2 essay better than 'People say …'.

items.prompt: Scientists expect that sea levels will rise by at least 30 cm this century. Rewrite starting 'Sea levels are …'
accepted_answers: Sea levels are expected to rise by at least 30 cm this century.
items.model_answer: Sea levels are expected to rise by at least 30 cm this century.
items.explanation: In the personal passive, the subject of the that-clause becomes the subject of the sentence, followed by 'be + past participle + to-infinitive': are expected to rise. The same pattern works with 'is thought to', 'is said to' and 'is believed to'.

items.prompt: Historians think that the first petrol-powered cars were produced in Germany in the 1880s. Rewrite starting 'The first petrol-powered cars are …'
accepted_answers: The first petrol-powered cars are thought to have been produced in Germany in the 1880s.
items.model_answer: The first petrol-powered cars are thought to have been produced in Germany in the 1880s.
items.explanation: When the belief is present but the event is past, use the perfect infinitive: are thought + to have been produced. The passive infinitive 'to have been + past participle' is needed because the cars did not produce themselves.

items.prompt: Someone should inform students about the risks of taking out large loans. (Use the passive with the modal verb.)
accepted_answers: Students should be informed about the risks of taking out large loans.
items.model_answer: Students should be informed about the risks of taking out large loans.
items.explanation: The modal passive is modal + be + past participle (should be informed, must be taught, could be reduced). It is very useful in Task 2 for recommendations when the agent is vague (someone, people, they).
